Thanks Rishi — helpful recap. A few clarifying items from our side before we onboard Legal with a redline: 

1) Controller / Processor: Confirm you will sign as Processor and that any directions we give will form the basis of processing activities.
2) Breach notice: our security policy requires notification to our security team within 72 hours of becoming aware of an incident impacting our data. Can Redwood commit to 72 hours for known data breaches involving PII?
3) Subprocessors: please provide a list with company name, role, location (country), and whether they are sub-processors that handle unencrypted content. We need that for our vendor review.
4) Data residency: We require that inference inputs and logs for EU customers be stored in EU-only infrastructure unless otherwise agreed. Please clarify which hosted models support EU residency, and if Dedicated/Private is required for full data residency.
5) Retention & deletion: For audit purposes we need confirmation that debug logs and request logs are retained for no longer than 90 days by default, and that we can request immediate deletion of all PII on contract termination.

Also please confirm whether you support Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or other transfer mechanisms for non-EU subprocessors.

I will loop in MedSys Legal if we get your answers and the subprocessors list.

Best,
Elena Koval
Head of Data Privacy, MedSys Health

Hi Elena / team — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and next steps.

1) Controller / Processor: Redwood will sign the DPA as Processor when acting to provide inference and hosting services. We accept controller instructions as set in the DPA and will not act outside documented instructions.

2) Breach notice timing: We are comfortable committing to a 72-hour notification window for confirmed incidents that impact customer data, subject to reasonable carve-outs for time to investigate and verify scope. Proposed contract language: "We will notify Controller without undue delay and, in any event, within 72 hours of confirming a data incident materially affecting Controller's data, except where additional time is reasonably required to identify the scope and remediate the incident."

3) Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessors export (subprocessors_list_2026-03-02.csv) showing vendor name, role, country, and whether they process unencrypted content. Redwood's policy is to provide 30 days notice of new subprocessors and to allow controllers to object on reasonable grounds.

4) Data residency: For full EU data residency (storage and processing within EU borders) we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. For our hosted offering we can route traffic and store logs in EU regions for customers on our EU region tenancy, but some background processing and certain managed services may still interact with non-EU infrastructure. We'll include explicit region routing options in the DPA and in the platform configuration section.

5) Retention & deletion: Default request/log retention is 90 days; we can include contractual limits and an option for shorter retention on Dedicated/Private. On termination, Controller can request certified deletion of all Customer Data; we'll confirm the deletion certificate process in the DPA.

6) International transfers: We support SCCs and EU-approved transfer mechanisms; we'll include SCC addendum language and note subprocessors subject to transfers.

Attachments: [Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (updated for EU residency clause)], [subprocessors_list_2026-03-02.csv], [SOC2_summary.pdf (redacted stub)].
